title: Pelvic anatomy, pelvic floor, Mullerian development and congenital anomalies

steps.say: The female internal reproductive organs develop from the paramesonephric or Mullerian ducts during early embryonic organogenesis. Lateral fusion of the caudal paired ducts forms the single uterovaginal canal, while canalization and midline septal resorption create the uterine cavity and upper two-thirds of the vagina.
steps.tx: Embryologically, the cranial non-fused **Mullerian ducts** form the fallopian tubes, while their caudal fused portions form the **uterovaginal canal** (uterus, cervix, and upper two-thirds of the vagina). The lower one-third of the vagina derives from the paired endodermal **sinovaginal bulbs** of the **urogenital sinus**, which canalize at the Mullerian tubercle to establish vaginal patency.

steps.say: Complete congenital agenesis of the paramesonephric ducts results in Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome. Affected adolescent females present with primary amenorrhoea and normal secondary sexual characteristics, exhibiting a 46,XX female karyotype and functionally normal ovaries, with frequent coexisting renal abnormalities.
steps.tx: **MRKH syndrome** (Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser) results from complete paramesonephric ductal aplasia, presenting as **primary amenorrhoea** in a phenotypic female with a 46,XX **normal karyotype**, functioning ovaries, absent uterus and upper vagina, and associated congenital **renal agenesis** or skeletal anomalies in 30 to 40 percent of patients.

left.title: MRKH Syndrome (Mullerian Agenesis)
points: Normal female ovaries; physiological serum estradiol and FSH
Absent uterus and upper vagina; normal pubic/axillary hair

right.title: Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (CAIS)
points: Internal undescended intra-abdominal or inguinal testes
Absent or sparse pubic and axillary hair due to androgen insensitivity

steps.say: Mullerian duct fusion and resorption failures yield diverse structural uterine anomalies. A septate uterus arises from incomplete resorption of the midline longitudinal fibrous septum, carrying the highest rate of first and second trimester spontaneous miscarriages, treatable by hysteroscopic metroplasty.
steps.tx: A **septate uterus** results from failure of midline resorption of the median Mullerian septum, representing the most common structural malformation associated with recurrent miscarriage (up to 70 percent loss rate). It is safely corrected surgically via outpatient **hysteroscopic metroplasty**, restoring a normal uterine cavity contour.

rows: Double uterus and cervix; high term birth rate

steps.say: The levator ani muscle complex forms the dynamic primary muscular support of the pelvic viscera. Consisting of the pubococcygeus, puborectalis, and iliococcygeus muscles, it maintains constant resting tone, closing the urogenital hiatus and supporting the bladder, vagina, and rectum.
steps.tx: The muscular pelvic diaphragm is formed by the **levator ani**, comprising the **puborectalis**, **pubococcygeus**, and **iliococcygeus** muscles. Innervated by the perineal branch of S4 and the pudendal nerve, it maintains resting closure of the **urogenital hiatus** against intra-abdominal pressure surges.

nodes.label: Puborectalis forms a U-shaped sling around the anorectal junction
Pubococcygeus bridges the pubic bone to the central perineal body
Iliococcygeus forms the broad posterolateral muscular shelf
Together maintain pelvic visceral suspension and fecal/urinary continence

steps.say: The perineal body serves as the crucial central fibromuscular hub of the perineum between the vagina and the anal canal. Spanning between the urogenital and anal triangles, it anchors the bulbospongiosus, superficial transverse perineal, and external anal sphincter muscles.
steps.tx: The **perineal body** is the central fibromuscular anchor situated between the vaginal introitus and anal canal. It provides essential structural convergence for the **bulbospongiosus**, **superficial transverse perineal**, external anal sphincter, and anterior pubococcygeus fibers, with its obstetrical disruption predisposing to pelvic organ prolapse.

left.title: Superficial Muscle Convergences
points: Superficial transverse perineal muscles stabilizing perineum
External anal sphincter maintaining voluntary fecal continence

right.title: Deep Muscular & Fascial Anchor
points: Deep transverse perineal muscle within urogenital diaphragm
Perineal membrane providing durable horizontal fascial support

steps.say: The ureter runs in close proximity to major pelvic vessels, making it susceptible to iatrogenic surgical injury during gynecological operations. The ureter passes immediately beneath the uterine artery within the cardinal ligament, crossing approximately one to two centimeters lateral to the supravaginal cervix.
steps.tx: During pelvic surgery, the **ureter** is vulnerable to iatrogenic ligation or transection where it passes directly inferior to the **uterine artery** ('water under the bridge') within the **cardinal ligament** (Mackenrodt's ligament), approximately 1.5 to 2 cm lateral to the supravaginal cervix.

nodes.label: Ureter enters true pelvis crossing the bifurcation of common iliac vessels
Runs along lateral pelvic sidewall anterior to internal iliac artery
Passes underneath uterine artery in the cardinal ligament tunnel
Pierces the trigone of the urinary bladder anterior to the vagina

steps.say: Endopelvic fascial condensations provide essential passive suspensory support for the uterus and upper vagina. Mackenrodt's cardinal ligaments anchor the lateral supravaginal cervix to the pelvic sidewalls, while the uterosacral ligaments anchor the cervix posteriorly to the sacral fascia.
steps.tx: Passive Level I pelvic organ suspension is achieved by the lateral **cardinal ligaments** (transverse cervical of Mackenrodt) anchoring to the pelvic sidewalls, and the **uterosacral ligaments** anchoring posteriorly from the supravaginal cervix to the S2-S4 **sacral fascia**, preventing apical vaginal descent and uterine prolapse.

rows: Apical prolapse (uterine prolapse, vaginal vault prolapse)
Endopelvic fascia to arcus tendineus fasciae pelvis
Anterior cystocele, lateral paravaginal wall detachment
Perineal body, perineal membrane, superficial muscles

steps.say: The lymphatic drainage of the female pelvic organs follows distinct vascular channels with vital oncological implications. The cervix and lower uterine segment drain laterally to obturator, internal iliac, and external iliac nodes, while the uterine fundus drains directly via ovarian vessels to para-aortic nodes.
steps.tx: **Lymphatic drainage** of the cervix and lower uterine segment travels laterally along parametrial vessels to the **obturator**, **internal iliac**, and **external iliac lymph nodes**. In contrast, the uterine fundus and cornua drain via the infundibulopelvic lymphatic pedicle directly into primary **para-aortic nodes**.
